title: The adaptation and validation of the Achievement Emotions Questionnaire for Physical Education-Elementary School
text:
Publications
        The adaptation and validation of the Achievement Emotions Questionnaire for Physical Education-Elementary School
        Mehmet Ceylan, Kevser Ceylan, Oğuzhan Yoncalık
      

      
        
          JournalInternational Journal of Assessment Tools in Education, 2026
          DOI10.21449/ijate.1730488
        
        Read the article
      

      
        In brief
        
          Young students feel enjoyment, anxiety and boredom in physical education, but few questionnaires suit their age. We adapted a brief questionnaire with visual support for third- and fourth-grade students and tested it with 772 children. It measured the three emotions reliably and as separate experiences. Measurement invariance was supported across gender. Across grades 3 and 4, configural, metric and scalar invariance were supported, while strict invariance was not fully supported.
        
      

      
        
          IssueVolume 13, issue 3, pp. 674–688
          First online2 April 2026
          Article typeScale adaptation and validation
          AccessOpen access; CC BY 4.0
          ThemesAchievement emotions; measurement and psychometrics
        
        
          Cite
          Data and materials
          Use this measure in Appendix 1 of the open-access article
        
        Summary drafted from the published article. Awaiting author approval.
      

      
        Research question
        Achievement emotions are emotions tied to learning activities and their outcomes. In physical education, enjoyment, anxiety and boredom relate to how motivated and engaged students are. Most questionnaires are written for older students.
        We asked whether a short, visually supported questionnaire could measure these three emotions validly among elementary school students in PE.

        What we did
        We translated the questionnaire forward and back, asked experts to check that each item kept its meaning, pre-tested the items for clarity, and piloted the visual layout. We then examined its structure with confirmatory factor analysis and exploratory structural equation modelling.
        
          Participants772 students (388 girls)
          Grades3 and 4
          Schools6 public elementary schools
          SamplingConvenience sample, one province
          AnalysesCFA, ESEM, multi-group CFA
          EthicsKırıkkale University Ethics Committee
        

        What we found
        
          The data supported three separate factors: enjoyment, anxiety and boredom. Model fit was strong, and items loaded clearly on their own factor with few cross-loadings.
          Reliability was satisfactory: Cronbach’s α and McDonald’s ω were above .70.
          Composite reliability exceeded .70 for all three factors. Average variance extracted was .452 for enjoyment, .566 for anxiety and .469 for boredom, so only anxiety reached the conventional .50 threshold. Discriminant validity among the three emotions was supported.
          Measurement invariance was supported across gender. Across grades 3 and 4, configural, metric and scalar invariance were supported; strict invariance was not fully supported.
        

        Why it matters
        
          For teachersA short questionnaire with pictures lets teachers check how young students feel in PE lessons without a long, text-heavy survey.
          For researchersScalar invariance across grades 3 and 4 supports comparing average levels of each emotion between these two grades.
        

        What this study does not show
        Students came from schools in a single province and were recruited as a convenience sample, so the results may not apply to other regions. All data came from students’ own reports. The study did not test external validity, such as links with other measures or outcomes. The questionnaire covers only enjoyment, anxiety and boredom, so it does not capture other emotions such as pride or shame.

        Cite this paper
        
          Ceylan, M., Ceylan, K., & Yoncalık, O. (2026). The adaptation and validation of the Achievement Emotions Questionnaire for Physical Education-Elementary School. International Journal of Assessment Tools in Education, 13(3), 674–688. https://doi.org/10.21449/ijate.1730488

title: Mehmet Ceylan
text:
Mehmet Ceylan
      I study how students feel in physical education—enjoyment, pride, boredom, anxiety—and how teaching, including the variety it offers, relates to their motivation and participation.
      
        Research Assistant, Department of Physical Education and Sport Teaching, Faculty of Sport Sciences, Kırıkkale University
        Visiting Research Scholar, Division of Kinesiology & Health, University of Wyoming, 2026–2027
      
      
        iDORCID
        Google Scholar
        Web of Science
        OSF
        ResearchGate
        LinkedIn
      
    

    
      Research
      
        
          
            What do students feel in physical education, and why?
            I study achievement emotions such as enjoyment, pride, boredom and anxiety in PE lessons. Using control-value theory, I ask how students’ sense of control and the value they see in PE relate to these emotions.
          
          
            How does variety in PE lessons relate to motivation and participation?
            I study variety support: teachers varying activities, equipment, groupings and tasks. I also ask whether variety works as a fourth basic psychological need, alongside autonomy, competence and relatedness.
          
          
            How can we measure students’ emotions in PE well?
            I adapt and validate questionnaires and observation tools for physical education, including a brief questionnaire for elementary school students.
